# glinet_tailscale (Resource)

Manages Tailscale on the router. The router has one Tailscale configuration, so use one instance of this resource. The login of the router to a tailnet is done one time in the web UI of the router and is not managed by this resource. When the router disables Tailscale, it also sets `lan_enabled` and `wan_enabled` to `false` and removes the exit node, so these can be set only when `enabled` is `true`. Destroy disables Tailscale on the router, which sets all values back to the initial state of the router. Tested on a router that was not logged in to a tailnet: what `lan_enabled`, `wan_enabled` and `exit_node_ip` do on a router that is logged in was not verified.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_tailscale" "this" {
  enabled     = true
  lan_enabled = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether Tailscale runs on the router (`enabled` in the router API).

### Optional

- `exit_node_ip` (String) Tailscale IPv4 or IPv6 address of the exit node that the router uses (`exit_node_ip` in the router API), for example `100.64.0.1` or `fd7a:115c:a1e0::1`. When it is not set, the router uses no exit node. Can be set only when `enabled` is `true`.
- `lan_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the devices in the tailnet can get remote access to the LAN of the router (`lan_enabled` in the router API). Can be `true` only when `enabled` is `true`. Defaults to `false`.
- `wan_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the devices in the tailnet can get remote access to the WAN of the router (`wan_enabled` in the router API). Can be `true` only when `enabled` is `true`. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `tailscale`.
- `lan_subnet` (String) The LAN subnet that the router advertises to the tailnet, for example `192.168.8.0/24` (`lan_ip` in the router API).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "tailscale".
terraform import glinet_tailscale.this tailscale
```
